Q. What regulatory advantage do self-funded health plans gain under ERISA?
[Answer]
ERISA exempts self-funded plans from state regulation, avoiding state benefit mandates and the ~ 2% state premium tax.

——————————
[Card 29 / 36]
Q. What are the two types of stop-loss insurance for a self-funded plan?
[Answer]
Specific (per individual) and aggregate (whole group, settled at year-end). Stop-loss protects the employer from catastrophic claims.

——————————
[Card 30 / 36]
Q. What does ERISA regulate, and what does it NOT require?
[Answer]
Federal law governing private employer benefit plans; sets minimum standards for participation, vesting, funding, and fiduciary responsibilities and pre-empts conflicting state laws. It does NOT require employers to provide benefits — it only regulates them if offered.

——————————
[Card 31 / 36]
Q. Which plans are exempt from ERISA, and what is a VEBA?
[Answer]
Governmental and church plans are exempt from ERISA. A VEBA (IRC §501(c)(9)) is a tax-exempt trust, established by an employer or through collective bargaining, that funds employee benefits; employer contributions to the trust are deductible.

——————————
[Card 32 / 36]
Q. How does unemployment insurance work and how are benefits taxed?
[Answer]
A federal-state joint program funded by employer FUTA/SUTA taxes. Covers involuntarily terminated employees (not those who quit or were fired for cause). Benefits typically last 26 weeks (extended during recessions) and are taxable income.

——————————
[Card 33 / 36]
Q. What is a group term life carve-out plan?
[Answer]
It removes older, higher-paid executives from the group term plan into individual coverage. Nondiscrimination rules don't apply to the carve-out, which can bring the base plan into compliance; the coverage is taxable to the employee.

——————————
[Card 34 / 36]
Q. What tests let a §79 group term life plan qualify (so key employees keep the $50,000 exclusion)?
[Answer]
Any ONE of: ≥70% of employees benefit; ≥85% of participants are not key employees; a nondiscriminatory classification; or, if in a cafeteria plan, §125 compliance.

——————————
[Card 35 / 36]
Q. What is a group survivor income benefit plan, and how is it taxed?
[Answer]
A monthly benefit paid to a surviving spouse/children (no beneficiary choice). It is taxable to recipients and is not treated as life insurance.

——————————
[Card 36 / 36]
Q. Name the three employer HRA arrangements and who each serves.
[Answer]
ICHRA (individual-coverage HRA — reimburses individual-market premiums), QSEHRA (qualified small-employer HRA — employers with



===== FP512 · M8 BUSINESS RISK SOLUTIONS =====

[18 cards]

——————————
[Card 1 / 18]
Q. Name the three basic steps of business risk management.
[Answer]
Risk identification, risk assessment, and risk control.

——————————
[Card 2 / 18]
Q. In business risk management, what does the risk identification step involve?
[Answer]
Defining the perils a business faces by its industry and size.

——————————
[Card 3 / 18]
Q. In business risk management, what does the risk assessment step involve?
[Answer]
Evaluating and weighing the risks that have been identified.

——————————
[Card 4 / 18]
Q. In business risk management, what does the risk control step involve?
[Answer]
Reductions, safety hardware, and procuring coverage.

——————————
[Card 5 / 18]
Q. Distinguish the businessowners policy (BOP) from the commercial package policy (CPP).
[Answer]
Both combine property and liability coverages from monoline forms at a discount. The BOP is designed for smaller businesses; the CPP is for larger companies. Commercial auto can be added to either.

——————————
[Card 6 / 18]
Q. What does directors' & officers' (D&O) insurance cover?
[Answer]
It is E&O coverage that protects a company's board members and officers.

——————————
[Card 7 / 18]
Q. What does Employment Practices Liability Insurance (EPLI) cover?
[Answer]
Wrongful termination, sexual harassment, and discrimination. Government fines are generally not covered.

——————————
[Card 8 / 18]
Q. Distinguish malpractice insurance from errors and omissions (E&O) insurance.
[Answer]
Malpractice covers physical harm (physicians, dentists, surgeons) and generally has no exclusion for intentional acts. E&O covers financial harm (accountants, lawyers, insurance agents, financial planners).

——————————
[Card 9 / 18]
Q. Who owns and benefits from key person insurance, and what is its purpose?
[Answer]
The business owns the policy and is the beneficiary; it provides working capital if a critical employee dies. The text recommends separate policies for business vs. personal needs.

——————————
[Card 10 / 18]
Q. How is key person insurance taxed?
[Answer]
Premiums are not deductible and the death benefit is not taxable.

——————————
[Card 11 / 18]
Q. Distinguish a cross-purchase buy-sell agreement from an entity-purchase buy-sell agreement.
[Answer]
Cross-purchase: owners individually buy policies on each other — control stays with the owners, but it is inefficient with more than two owners. Entity-purchase: the business buys the policies — easier to administer, but control shifts to the business.

——————————
[Card 12 / 18]
Q. What is a Life Insurance Retirement Plan (LIRP) and how is it funded?
[Answer]
A LIRP uses a permanent (whole or universal life) policy to fund retirement, mimicking Roth tax treatment with no income limits. It cannot be funded with term life, and it is not subject to ERISA.

——————————
[Card 13 / 18]
Q. What two cautions apply when using a LIRP?
[Answer]
Watch the MEC rules and avoid lapsing the policy.

——————————
[Card 14 / 18]
Q. What two general categories of cyberattack exist?
[Answer]
Malware (covert spyware) and phishing (social engineering).

——————————
[Card 15 / 18]
Q. What measures help reduce cyber insurance premiums?
[Answer]
Employee security training, multi-factor authentication, and a disaster recovery plan.

——————————
[Card 16 / 18]
Q. Distinguish cyber insurance from fraud/crime (fidelity) insurance.
[Answer]
Cyber covers data breach, ransomware, and related business interruption. Fraud/crime (fidelity) covers employee or third-party dishonesty, embezzlement, and forgery. They are distinct policies.

——————————
[Card 17 / 18]
Q. What are a PEO and an AHP, and what do they let small employers do?
[Answer]
A PEO (Professional Employer Organization) and an AHP (Association Health Plan) let small and medium employers pool together to access large-group benefits and administration.

——————————
[Card 18 / 18]
Q. Which 'monoline' coverage forms can a commercial package policy (CPP) bundle?
[Answer]
Commercial property, boiler & machinery (equipment breakdown), crime, inland marine/transportation, commercial general liability, commercial auto, and workers' compensation.
